correctness.rationale: The singleton image of any atom cannot be the universal target point: back would require two disjoint-colored sets meeting that singleton, contradicting forth. The image of each subset is then forced by its atom colors; back excludes a universal image of a monochromatic set. Every resulting two-coloring is surjective because the target back-neighborhood graph is connected. Conversely direct-image maps satisfy forth and back for all subsets, finite or infinite. The adjunction and counts follow; exhaustive finite enumeration independently checks one through four source atoms.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete morphism classification in the finite and infinite atomic Boolean compatibility frames of recent modal-forcing research. Its nontrivial direction shows that no abstract frame p-morphisms onto the smallest nontransitive co-consistency target exist except direct images of atom bipartitions; equivalently, every such relational quotient is uniquely adjoint to a Boolean partition embedding. Exact hom-set sizes follow. This structural rigidity has a clear role in understanding permissible full-frame quotients and does not claim a separate axiomatization or an arbitrary downstream theorem.
